children.name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
children.blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the process of matching on-chain transaction records with internal accounting ledgers for digital assets.

children.name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
children.blurb: Valuing illiquid tokens covers digital assets that do not trade on an active market with reliable volume.

children.name: Auditing Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Auditing smart contracts is the practice of reviewing the code, state transitions, and economic logic of programs that execute on a blockchain.

children.name: Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries
children.blurb: Accounting for decentralised treasuries covers the recording, valuation, and reporting of assets held by DAOs, protocol treasuries, and other on-chain entities that manage funds through smart contracts and multisig wallets.

children.name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
children.blurb: Impairment of unique digital assets covers how entities test and write down the carrying value of non-fungible tokens, digital collectibles, virtual land, in-game items, and similar one-of-a-kind intangible assets recorded on a blockchain.

sections.body: Digital asset accounting is the work of recording, valuing, and reporting blockchain based assets and obligations inside an organisation's books. In practice, AI is used to match on chain transactions to ledger entries, flag anomalies, classify wallets, and estimate fair value when markets are thin. It also helps audit smart contracts by scanning code and transaction histories for patterns that human reviewers might miss. The field sits between accounting standards, cryptography, and data engineering, so the models rarely work alone. They depend on clean data, clear custody rules, and human judgement about intent and control.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The site tracks 215 compliance and regulation pages, and that volume reflects how much of digital asset accounting is about meeting reporting rules rather than only about the technology. Reconciliation of high volume, well labelled wallet activity can be automated with rules and machine learning, and smart contract auditing has mature static analysis tools alongside newer AI assistants. What is not solved is valuation, because illiquid tokens have no reliable market price and models that infer value from comparable assets or liquidity pools can be wrong. Impairment for unique digital assets is also hard because each item may be one of a kind and may have no active market. Decentralised treasuries add governance and timing problems, since spending may be approved by token votes and recorded across multiple chains. The honest limit is that AI can produce a defensible estimate, not a certain number, and auditors still need evidence and disclosure.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section follow the accounting lifecycle from raw chain data to reported impairment. Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation covers the first step, bringing wallet and exchange activity into a general ledger and resolving timing and fee differences. Valuing Illiquid Tokens deals with the next problem, estimating fair value when there is little or no trading volume. Auditing Smart Contracts focuses on the code layer, checking logic, permissions, and known vulnerability patterns before value is trusted. Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries looks at how groups hold and spend digital assets through governance processes rather than a single corporate bank account. Impairment of Unique Digital Assets closes the sequence by asking when a one of a kind token or collectible must be written down and how that write down is supported, so a reader can move through these pages in order or go directly to the one that matches the asset and control question at hand.
